description: Nevada-only rules checked against the cited Nevada Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Nevada makes it unlawful to drive, in any event, faster than
questions.explanation: NRS 484B.600(1)(e) says it is unlawful to drive at a rate of speed greater than 80 miles per hour in any event. That absolute cap is separate from the basic reasonable-speed rule and from posted limits.

questions.q: In a designated Nevada school crossing zone, the statutory speed is
questions.explanation: NRS 484B.363(2) sets 25 miles per hour in a school crossing zone, with the same exceptions as subsection 1: school not in session, a subsection 6 period, a beacon that is not flashing the limit into effect, or a sign showing the limit is not in effect.

questions.q: On highways it builds and maintains, the Nevada Department of Transportation
options: must post 80 mph on every rural freeway
may set up to 80 mph, or lower for safety
may not set any limit above 65 mph
has no authority to set speeds
questions.explanation: NRS 484B.613 says NDOT may establish speed limits on highways it constructs and maintains, not to exceed 80 miles per hour, and may set a lower limit where needed for public health and safety or for trucks, overweight and oversized vehicles, trailers, and buses. Eighty is a ceiling the department may use, not an automatic statewide freeway speed.

questions.q: Under the current Nevada DUI statute, it is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.08 or more in blood or breath, including a test within 2 hours
any measurable amount if the driver is 21 or older
questions.explanation: The current text of NRS 484C.110, the version effective until repeal of the federal 0.08 highway-funding condition, makes it unlawful to drive with 0.08 or more in blood or breath, or to be found by measurement within 2 hours after driving to have 0.08 or more. The contingent 0.10 version is not the current text.

questions.q: Driving a commercial motor vehicle in Nevada is unlawful at an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.08 only, the same as a car
any amount, with no numeric threshold
questions.explanation: Current NRS 484C.120, effective until repeal of the federal 0.08 funding condition, makes it unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with 0.04 or more but less than 0.08 in blood or breath, including a measurement within 2 hours after driving. The contingent text that uses 0.10 is not current.

questions.q: If a Nevada driver under 21 tests at 0.02 or more but less than 0.08, the license, permit, or driving privilege
options: must be revoked for one year
questions.explanation: Current NRS 483.461 says that if a test under NRS 484C.150 or 484C.160 shows a person under 21 had 0.02 or more but less than 0.08, the license, permit, or privilege must be suspended for 90 days. The version that uses 0.10 instead of 0.08 takes effect only if the federal 0.08 funding law is repealed.

questions.q: A Nevada driver's first accumulation of 12 demerit points in a 12-month period causes
options: a 1-year revocation with no restricted license
cancellation of the license until age 21
questions.explanation: NRS 483.475(3)(a) suspends the license for 6 months for the first accumulation of 12 demerit points during a 12-month period. That driver is eligible for a restricted license during the suspension. This is the licensed-driver rule, not the separate future-driving-privileges section.

questions.q: Nevada's uniform demerit schedule runs
options: From 1 demerit to 8 demerits, by severity
From 2 points to 12 points, with no ceiling
A flat 3 points for every moving violation
Only DUI convictions, with no point scale
questions.explanation: NRS 483.473 requires a uniform system based on accumulation during 12 months, on a scale of one demerit for a minor traffic violation to eight demerits for an extremely serious violation. If two or more violations are committed on a single occasion, points are assessed only for the offense with the greater point value.

questions.q: When a Nevada licensee has 3 or more demerit points but fewer than 12, the Department
options: notifies the person of the points
questions.explanation: NRS 483.475(1) requires notice at 3 or more but less than 12 demerit points. If the driver then proves completion of an approved traffic-safety course that was not required by a plea agreement or a court order under NRS 484A.7043, the Department cancels not more than 3 demerits. The course may be used once in 12 months. If the driver reaches 12 points before finishing the course, the points are not cancelled and the license is suspended.

questions.q: A third Nevada accumulation, within 5 years, of 12 demerit points in a 12-month period means
options: a 6-month suspension with a restricted license
a 1-year suspension with no restricted license
no suspension if a course was taken earlier
questions.explanation: NRS 483.475(3)(c) sets that third accumulation within 5 years at a 1-year suspension. The driver is not eligible for a restricted license during that suspension. A second accumulation within 3 years is also 1 year, but that driver remains eligible for a restricted license.

questions.q: Before a 16- or 17-year-old gets a Nevada license, the supervised driving log must show at least
questions.explanation: NRS 483.2521(1)(b) requires at least 50 hours of supervised driving with a restricted license, instruction permit, or restricted instruction permit, including at least 10 hours during darkness, unless a subsection 3 defensive-driving substitute applies.

questions.q: For the first 6 months of a Nevada license issued at 16 or 17, the driver shall not transport
questions.explanation: NRS 483.2523(1) says a person licensed under NRS 483.2521 shall not, during the first 6 months after the license is issued, transport a passenger under 18 unless the passenger is a member of the driver's immediate family. The sections opened do not set a nighttime curfew.

questions.q: In Nevada, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Nevada issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Nevada car permit: 15½ years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Nevada, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Nevada requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: Of a Nevada teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Nevada requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Nevada: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: NRS 483.2521 Drivers who are 16 or 17 years of age: Prerequisites to issuance of license

questions.q: In Nevada, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Nevada, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: NRS 483.2521 Drivers who are 16 or 17 years of age: Prerequisites to issuance of license

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Nevada not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Nevada restricts provisional drivers from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Nevada new drivers: off the road 10 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: In Nevada, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Nevada drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Nevada car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Nevada car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Nevada car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Nevada car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Nevada, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Nevada, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Nevada, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: NRS: CHAPTER 484C - DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ALCOHOL OR A PROHIBITED SUBSTANCE

questions.q: In Nevada, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Nevada sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: NRS 483.461 Mandatory suspension of license of person less than 21 years of age if test shows concentration of alcohol of 0.02 or more but less than 0.08 in blood or breath

questions.q: In Nevada, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Nevada brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Nevada, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

provenance.manual: NRS 484C.210 Revocation of license, permit or privilege to drive when person fails to submit to evidentiary test

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Nevada residential district?
questions.explanation: Nevada sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Nevada?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Nevada can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Nevada rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Nevada's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Nevada: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: How is Nevada's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Nevada seat belt enforcement is secondary.

provenance.manual: NRS 484D.495 Safety belts and shoulder harness assembly; requirements for driver, child and other passenger; penalties; exemptions

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Nevada?
questions.explanation: Nevada requires a car seat or booster until 6 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Nevada: car or booster seat until 6 years.

questions.q: What is Nevada's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Nevada requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $20,000.

questions.q: Under Nevada's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Nevada can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
